technology roadmap. As you all have noticed, we have commercialized 3 
new products this quarter, helical limited slip differential for passenger cars 
and SUVs, air springs for railways, and a rear radar sensor for two-wheelers.  
 
The first product is helical limited slip differential. A limited slip differential or 
what we call LSD improves vehicle traction by limiting excess speed 
difference between the two driven wheels. Helical limited slip differential is a 
type of LSD that uses parallel axis helical pinions interacting with the side 
gears to generate internal axial and radial forces. This passive mechanism 
delivers smooth, progressive torque transfer without a conventional clutch 
pack or external actuation. LSDs are typically used in performance vehicles, 
off-road SUVs, and 4x4s.

The next product is air spring, air springs are used in most modern railway 
coaches, including LHB coaches. These coaches use a two-state suspension 
system. The primary suspension uses coil springs to filter high frequency track 
vibrations, while the air spring forms the secondary suspension connecting 
the bogie to the coach body. Airsprings enhance passenger comfort, 
maintain a constant ride height, and isolate body movement. Together with 
the dampers, which control oscillations, they provide a smoother and safer 
ride at high speeds.  
 
The 3rd product is a rear radar sensor for 2-wheelers. 2 wheelers are amongst 
the most vulnerable vehicles on the road, making timely warnings critical to 
rider safety. A rear radar sensor does precisely that, by warning the rider of a 
potential rear end collision or a vehicle in a blind spot. It provides valuable 
time to maneuver to a safer position. As a pioneer in automotive radar, we 
recognized early the potential for applying this technology for two-wheelers. 
Together with safety systems this product can make a meaningful
